step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture illustrates Telecoming's Aquarius automated testing system. An EC2 instance serves as an orchestrator connected to an RDS database storing test configurations. The tests are executed as Selenium browser simulations on AWS Fargate Spot managed via Amazon ECS, scaling up to handle thousands of tests with up to 70% cost savings. Execution reports and results are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket, which are subsequently fetched and displayed by an internal Intranet dashboard web application. AWS Enterprise Support provides proactive architecture advisement.

graph.name: Telecoming Aquarius Automated Testing Architecture
graph.notes: Telecoming's Aquarius platform automates web simulation testing using EC2, RDS, ECS Fargate Spot, S3, and an internal Intranet dashboard.

nodes.name: EC2 Orchestrator
nodes.notes: Orchestrates test configurations and connects to RDS database.

nodes.name: RDS Database
nodes.notes: Stores test configurations for 200-400 concurrent test executions.

nodes.name: Amazon ECS
nodes.notes: Container orchestrator for running test tasks on Fargate.

nodes.name: Fargate Spot
nodes.notes: Runs Selenium testing tasks serverlessly using Spot instances, performing ~30,000 daily tests at ~70% cost savings.

nodes.name: S3 Execution Storage
nodes.notes: Stores execution reports and test output artifacts.

nodes.name: Intranet
nodes.notes: Internal web application used by teams to visualize test quality and reports.

nodes.name: Enterprise Support
nodes.notes: AWS Enterprise Support advising on architecture optimization such as Fargate Spot.

edges.notes: EC2 orchestrator queries RDS for test configurations.
Configurations trigger automated test execution on Fargate Spot containers.
Fargate Spot tasks output execution results to S3.
Intranet web app retrieves test results from S3 for internal monitoring.
